title: What distinct() actually does
description: You called distinct(). Spark has not read a row. Rebuild the plan from that call through the shuffle.

problemStatement.overview:
Finance wanted unique rows. Someone wrote `df.distinct()` and then hit `.count()`.

Until that action, Spark had not read a single partition. `distinct()` is lazy — Catalyst only recorded an Aggregate whose grouping keys are every column.

The physical plan is not one global unique pass. It is two HashAggregates with a shuffle between them: map-side local unique, a shuffle on all columns, then reduce-side global unique.

The outline of that plan is already on the board. Fill each empty block from Unused. Widgets that do not belong are traps. Spill is real, but optional.
problemStatement.yourTask: Fill each empty block with the operator that belongs there. The wires are already drawn.
yourTaskSteps: Read every widget. They all look equally plausible.
Drop an operator onto each empty block — or select a widget, then click a block.
The dashed block is optional. Leave it empty, or place spill there.
Submit. Wrong operators and traps fail. The outline of the plan is given; the labels are not.
hints: distinct() is lazy. An action is what asks for a physical plan.
The physical plan is two HashAggregates with a shuffle between them.
The same row can live in many partitions, so local unique is not global unique.
problemStatement.moat:
Setter notes — not shown to learners.

Board lab. sandboxType=board. No cluster. Gold is a DAG (parent → child), not fixed lanes.

Required chain:
lazy-agg → action-fires → physical-two-agg → map-scan → bytes-to-bytes-map → shuffle-all-cols → reduce-global

Optional splice: spill-merge on bytes-to-bytes-map → shuffle-all-cols.

Seven traps must stay unused. Grade lives in backend/workspace/boardGrade.ts.

pieces.title: Lazy Aggregate — all columns are keys
pieces.blurb: df.distinct() is a transform. Catalyst records an Aggregate whose grouping keys are every column. No data is read yet.

pieces.title: An action builds the physical plan
pieces.blurb: .count(), .show(), or .write() is what asks Catalyst for a physical plan. distinct() itself does not.

pieces.title: HashAggregate → Shuffle → HashAggregate
pieces.blurb: The physical plan is two aggregations with a shuffle between them — not one global unique pass.

pieces.title: Map task scans its partition
pieces.blurb: Each executor task reads only the rows in its assigned partition, row by row.

pieces.title: BytesToBytesMap (local unique)
pieces.blurb: Spark hashes the whole row into a Tungsten BytesToBytesMap. Same hash and same bytes → drop immediately.

pieces.title: Spill + external merge-sort
pieces.blurb: If the map fills, rows are sorted by hash, spilled, and merge-sorted so local duplicates still die. Correctness does not require this card.

pieces.title: Shuffle: hash-partition on all columns
pieces.blurb: Surviving local-unique rows are hashed on the entire row so identical rows from different maps land on the same reducer.

pieces.title: Reduce-side map (global unique)
pieces.blurb: Each reducer merges incoming rows into a final hash map and emits rows that are unique across the cluster.

pieces.title: distinct() executes at the call
pieces.blurb: Calling df.distinct() scans the dataset immediately and returns unique rows before any action.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: distinct() is lazy. An action is required.

pieces.title: Driver builds one global hash set
pieces.blurb: Executors send every row to the driver, which uniques them in one HashSet and broadcasts the result.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: Uniques are computed on executors, not collected to the driver.

pieces.title: Broadcast the unique rows
pieces.blurb: After local dedup, the unique set is broadcast to every executor so each task can filter against it.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: distinct() shuffles on the row, it does not broadcast the set.

pieces.title: Global sort, then drop adjacent dups
pieces.blurb: Spark range-partitions, sorts each partition, and drops equal neighbors — like sort | uniq.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: Default distinct is hash-aggregate, not sort-based.

pieces.title: Shuffle on the first column only
pieces.blurb: The shuffle key is the leftmost column. Other columns are compared only after rows arrive.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: Grouping and shuffle keys are every column, not a subset.

pieces.title: Local unique is enough — no shuffle
pieces.blurb: If each partition drops its own duplicates, the dataset is already globally unique.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: The same row can live in many partitions. Shuffle is required.

pieces.title: Distinct is a pushed-down filter
pieces.blurb: Catalyst rewrites distinct() as a Filter on the scan so duplicates never leave the file source.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: Filter ≠ Distinct. This is an Aggregate, not a predicate.
